value.name: Homozygous GDAP1 Ser194Ter patient-derived motor neurons
value.description: Motor neurons from one homozygous Ser194Ter CMT2H patient were compared with two unrelated controls. Lower GDAP1 mRNA/protein, perturbed cristae and increased MitoSOX signal were observed; significance for MitoSOX was reached versus one control only. ATP content was not significantly different, which does not establish normal respiratory flux. Nonsense-mediated decay and apoptosis were proposed without direct demonstration. This is a recessive comparison model with no isogenic rescue.
The recessive patient culture shares a ROS-related endpoint with some dominant cell models.
value.limitations: One recessive donor and two unrelated controls; not a model of dominant fusion interference. Significance depends on the control comparison.

value.name: Dominant GDAP1 patient fibroblast redox and respiration study
value.description: Six patient lines came from two unrelated families: three C240Y and three R120W. Available lines and controls varied by assay. Complex-I-substrate respiration and ATP synthesis were lower in both groups, but direct complex I enzyme and oxidative-stress abnormalities were clearest in C240Y. Complex I assembly and NDUFB8 abundance were preserved; SIRT1/NRF1 abundance decreased without a mediation experiment. Resveratrol treatment for 48 hours improved pooled complex I activity at 25 micromolar; 10 micromolar had no significant effect and 50 micromolar was antiproliferative. No clinical benefit or universal GST-domain severity rule was demonstrated.

assertion.description: C240Y fibroblasts had reduced complex I enzyme activity.
assertion.limitations: Only two families; R120W enzyme-activity reduction was nonsignificant. No isogenic correction.

value.name: Gdap1-null primary motor and sensory neuron cultures

value.name: Human DHX37 depletion and catalytic-mutant complementation
value.description: HeLa RNAi and HEK293 complementation with RNAi-resistant wild-type or engineered T282A DHX37 define pre-rRNA processing and small-subunit assembly functions. Wild-type transgene rescues processing defects. Purified recombinant-protein experiments independently show RNA-dependent ATPase activity and stimulation by directly interacting UTP14A. The catalytic mutant retains the protein-presence function that prevents aberrant pre-rRNA turnover, separating that function from ATPase-dependent maturation.

The exact stage of human U3 release remains unresolved, and UTP14A-depletion effects on U3 retention may be secondary to an earlier processing block.

value.name: Organoid-derived Pseudomonas pneumonia-on-a-chip (VAP) model
value.description: An alveolus chip lined with organoid-derived alveolar epithelial cells that differentiate into both type 2 and type 1-like cells, plus primary pulmonary microvascular endothelium, cycled at a respiratory-like 0.25 Hz at either physiological (5%) or hyperphysiological (10%) strain and infected with Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Comparing the two strain levels under an otherwise identical infection isolates the contribution of ventilation-associated stretch, which is the central question in ventilator-associated pneumonia and ventilator-induced lung injury.
value.cell_source: Human alveolar organoid-derived epithelial cells and primary pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells
value.culture_system: Alveolus-on-a-chip with air-liquid interface, vascular flow, and controlled cyclic strain

assertion.description: Raising cyclic strain from physiological to hyperphysiological levels increased apparent permeability and, under infection, increased bacterial counts in the vascular channel. This reproduces the clinical interaction in which ventilation-associated overdistension worsens an infectious insult rather than merely coexisting with it.
assertion.limitations: Uniform cyclic strain across a chip membrane is not the regionally heterogeneous overdistension and cyclic recruitment-derecruitment of an injured ventilated lung, and the model has no immune cells, so the leukocyte-mediated component of ventilator-induced injury is absent. Readouts are at 12 hours post-infection only.

readouts.name: Apparent permeability under hyperphysiological versus physiological strain
readouts.interpretation: Strain-dependent permeability increase is the barrier readout for stretch injury.

readouts.name: Bacterial translocation to the vascular channel under increased strain
readouts.interpretation: Higher vascular-channel colony counts under greater strain quantify the strain-infection interaction.

selected_evidence.snippet: We hereby present what we believe to be the first functional Pseudomonas POC and VAP-on-a-chip model that replicates key features of disease, including enhanced mechanical strain.

value.name: Human airway-on-a-chip chlorine gas exposure model
value.description: A microfluidic human airway chip with pseudostratified mucociliary epithelium, a biomimetic extracellular matrix hydrogel, an endothelial compartment, and integrated electrodes for transepithelial electrical resistance, coupled to a chlorine generation and delivery platform that controls concentration and exposure duration precisely. It addresses a gap that is unusually hard to fill any other way: human clinical data on acute chlorine exposure are scarce for obvious reasons, and animal models translate poorly.

assertion.limitations: Chlorine is one specific inhalational insult and the chip is bronchial rather than alveolar, so it models the direct pulmonary insult category only for inhaled oxidant gases and not for aspiration, pneumonia, or the indirect systemic insults that cause most ARDS.
